title: Fair Commodity Taxation
abstract: arXiv:2604.19044v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: We study optimal taxation in monopoly screening problems with a redistribution-minded regulator. When the regulator moves before the monopolist, any nondecreasing allocation can be implemented as the monopolist's optimum under an appropriate tax schedule. Despite this flexibility, we show that our redistribution-minded regulator never strictly benefits from randomization or nonlinear taxes. Under a strengthening of Myersonian regularity, which we call strong regularity, we characterize the tax rates on the fairness-efficiency frontier: it is enough for the regulator to consider policies which consist of a per-unit excise tax and a lump-sum rebate, with all (and only) tax rates between the consumer-surplus maximizing rate and the Laffer peak appearing on the frontier. Finally, we show subsidies are never used, and that every frontier threshold policy rations more than the unregulated monopolist.

translated_abstract: 我们研究了在垄断甄别问题中，具有再分配意愿的监管者的最优税收问题。当监管者先于垄断者行动时，任何非递减的配置都可以在适当的税收方案下作为垄断者的最优选择被实施。尽管存在这种灵活性，我们证明了具有再分配意愿的监管者永远不会从随机化或非线性税收中严格获益。在迈尔森正则性的加强版本（我们称之为“强正则性”）下，我们刻画了公平-效率前沿上的税率：监管者只需考虑由单位消费税和一次性返还组成的政策，且所有（且仅有）介于消费者剩余最大化税率与拉弗峰值之间的税率会出现在前沿上。最后，我们证明补贴从不被使用，并且前沿上的每一个门槛政策都比不受监管的垄断者实施更多的配给。
tldr: 该论文证明，在垄断甄别问题中，再分配型监管者无需随机化或非线性税收，仅通过单位消费税加一次性返还的简单政策即可实现公平与效率前沿，且前沿上的所有税率都位于消费者剩余最大化税率与拉弗峰值之间。
en_tdlr: This paper proves that a redistribution-minded regulator in monopoly screening needs neither randomization nor nonlinear taxes: simple per-unit excise taxes with lump-sum rebates trace the entire fairness-efficiency frontier, with all frontier tax rates lying between the consumer-surplus-maximizing rate and the Laffer peak.
